Disappointing and overpriced for what’s offered
Dec 2025 • Couples
We were really looking forward to eating at Braai Pit, especially as South Africans hoping for familiar flavours, but unfortunately the experience was very disappointing.

Service was extremely slow from the start despite the place being empty and only having 1-2 additional patrons by the time we left. Even simple coffees took a long time to arrive and did not come out together. Overall waiting times were long across the board.

The biggest let-down was the braaibroodjie. It was more expensive than the other toasted sandwich options (I assumed because of the special, more complicated way in which they're made), yet when it arrived it was essentially just a barely toasted sandwich. The tomato and cheese inside were still cold and the cheese had not even begun to melt. We sent it back and asked for it to be made hotter. When it was eventually returned, we were given a very dirty look, which made the situation uncomfortable. The sandwich was the first and then last item to come out and was still just a basic toasted sandwich. This is not what South Africans know or expect a braaibroodjie to be.

The mixed grill meat breakfast was okay but nothing memorable. The steak was good and probably the highlight of the meal. The chicken schnitzel was extremely thin, tough and dry. Slap chips were acceptable and did have a good amount of vinegar, which we appreciated. Coffees were not bad but again very slow.

What made this more disappointing is that we arrived hungry and still left a significant amount of food uneaten, simply because it was not enjoyable. Overall, the experience did not justify the price. For a place positioning itself around South African food, it missed the mark on flavour, execution and hospitality. Sadly, it did not hit the spot in terms of South African taste or service and we would not return. There are other, far better options to enjoy in Da Nang.

Braaipit is a hidden gem in Danang's culinary scene. This South African restaurant offers a delightful experience for meat lovers. 

The cozy ambiance and attentive service create a welcoming atmosphere. 

The highlight of Braaipit is undoubtedly the perfectly grilled meats. From succulent lamb chops to juicy boerewors sausages, each dish is bursting with flavor. The menu also features traditional sides and amazing biltong and droewors , adding to the overall experience. 

The prices was very reasonable and generous portions, Braaipit is a must-visit for those seeking a unique and mouthwatering dining adventure in Danang.

Fantastic Food at Braii Pit Hoi An
Jun 2022
Although this is the site for the Braai Pit in Da Nang, unfortunately their new sister restaurant in Hoi An is not yet listed on Trip Advisor, so I am writing the review here instead, as they are the same company. Braai Pit Hoi An is a small, cosy bar and restaurant with a good range of drinks, super warm welcoming owners, managers and staff in general and amongst the best tasting food in Hoi An. As we were only there for a week we wouldn't normally eat in the same place more than once, just to ring the changes, but we kept going back there as the food was so tasty, the atmosphere so welcoming and there was good live music during the evenings. It was also not too loud so you could still have a conversation with friends. I would heartily recommend the sweet and sour chicken - this is the real deal - not half baked naked chicken but proper crispy batter to a fine texture. When I first saw that it was served with a cold dip in sweet and sour sauce I was disappointed as I had imagined a hot sweet and sour sauce with onions, pineapple and green peppers, served on a bed of rice. But it was so exceptionally delicious that I found myself enjoying the cold sauce with the piping hot crispy battered chicken balls , as much as the usual way it is presented. Rice was not listed on the menu at all but after asking if it was possible to have any, it appeared hot and steaming with the sweet and sour chicken, the owner explaining that they had gone to buy some specially. To me this was one of the ultimates in customer service and highly appreciated by us. We only had chance to eat the chicken in bread crumbs, salad and french fries too but the chicken was enormous, the breadcrumb exterior hot and crispy and the french fries piping hot too. Whenever I return to Hoi An I will definitely make a bee line for the sweet and sour chicken first and then make enough visits to work my way through that awesome tasting menu.
